parsed.explanation: Section 3 proves exactly what its header says: V contains at most one POSITIVE value (the argument starts 'Suppose V contains two distinct positive numbers c1 > c2 > 0'). From this alone the stated dichotomy — 'either g ≡ 0 or V ⊆ {0, c}' — does not follow: negative values are never excluded, and the only bound the text records is g(x) > -x. The needed lemma g ≥ 0 (one line: x + n·g(x) = fⁿ(x) > 0 for all n forces g(x) ≥ 0) appears nowhere in the write-up. The gap is load-bearing: Lemma 1 explicitly uses 'b = g(z) ∈ {0, c} (because V ⊆ {0, c})', and the S_0/S_c level-set analysis and covering argument of §§4–6 all presuppose V ⊆ {0, c}. Hence the necessity argument (upper_bound) is incomplete as written, though the fix is a routine one-line orbit-positivity argument.
